questions.question: In which year was the Second Anglo-Burma War fought?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1852.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Causes triggered by disputes over trade, British expansionist policies, and the mistreatment of British merchants in Burma territory.
 
• Outcome resulted in a decisive British victory and the annexation of Lower Burma, including the key port city of Rangoon (Yangon).
 
• Impact strengthened British control over Burma, making it a significant part of British India and laying the groundwork for further conflict leading to the **Third Anglo-Burma War in 1885.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The war was relatively short, lasting a few months in **1852,** and was largely fought over control of strategic trade routes and territorial dominance.
 
• The British forces, led by General Godwin, easily overpowered the Burma forces due to superior weaponry and military tactics.
 
• The annexation of Lower Burma increased British control over valuable resources like teak and oil and established dominance over key trade routes in Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadratha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Brihadratha Maurya was the final ruler of the Mauryan dynasty, reigning from around **187 BCE to 180 BCE.**
 
• He was assassinated by his own general,** Pushyamitra Shunga**, during a military parade.
 
• His reign marked the further disintegration of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• His death ended the Mauryan Empire, a significant era in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Bindusara:**

__
 
• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta Maurya, ruled from around **297 BCE to 273 BCE.**
 
• He maintained strong diplomatic relations with foreign kingdoms, such as the Seleucid Empire and the Hellenistic world, which helped in trade and political stability.
 
• Bindusara was the** father of Ashoka **the Great, and his reign set the stage for Ashoka’s future expansion and the spread of Buddhism.

**Ashoka:**

 
• 
 After the Kalinga War, Ashoka embraced Buddhism and adopted a policy of** non-violence.**
 
 
• 
 He promoted **Buddhism **across Asia through missionary work and built numerous stupas and pillars.
 
 
• Ashoka focused on **public welfare, social justice,** and religious tolerance through his edicts and policies.

**Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
• Founder of the Mauryan Empire,he established the Mauryan Empire around **321 BCE**, unifying most of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Chandragupta defeated the **Nanda Dynasty in Magadha **with the guidance of his mentor, Chanakya.
 
• In his later years, he abdicated the throne, embraced **Jainism**, and reportedly fasted to death at Shravanabelagola.

• Declined after Ashoka’s death, weakened by internal strife, and ended around **185 BCE **with the assassination of the last ruler,** Brihadratha**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct about the Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023?

I. The Bill will apply to the processing of digital personal data within India where such data is collected online or collected offline and is digitized.

II. It will also apply to such processing outside India, if it is for offering goods or services in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3) Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Scope of the Bill:** The Digital Personal Data Protection Bill, 2023 applies to the processing of digital personal data both within and outside India.
 
• **Data Collection:** The Bill covers data collected both online and offline that is subsequently digitized.
 
• **Cross-Border Data Processing:** The Bill also extends to data processing outside India if the processing is related to offering goods or services in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purpose:** The Bill aims to protect the privacy and security of individuals' personal data.
 
• **Key Provisions:** The Bill includes provisions related to data collection, storage, usage, sharing, and transfer of personal data.
 
• **Data Fiduciary:** The Bill defines a data fiduciary as a person or entity that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data.
 
• **Individual Rights:** The Bill provides individuals with various rights, such as the right to access, rectify, erase, and restrict the processing of their personal data.
 
• **Data Breach Notification:** Data fiduciaries are required to notify individuals and the government in case of a data breach.

questions.question: The government of India in Budget 2023-24, has adopted how many priorities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of India in Budget 2023-24 has adopted **seven priorities**.
 
• They are named as **SAPTRISHI**.
 
• These priorities are aimed at driving economic growth, enhancing infrastructure, and improving the overall quality of life for citizens.
 
• The seven priorities reflect the government's focus on areas such as
 
 
• inclusive development,
 
• reaching the last mile,
 
• infrastructure and investment,
 
• unleashing the potential,
 
• green growth,
 
• youth power, and
 
• financial sector.
 
 
 
• These priorities are expected to provide a comprehensive framework for the country's development agenda in the coming fiscal year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inclusive Development**: Ensuring equitable growth across various sectors and sections of society.
 
• **Reaching the Last Mile**: Targeting development initiatives to benefit the most marginalized communities.
 
• **Infrastructure and Investment**: Enhancing physical and digital infrastructure to boost economic activity.
 
• **Unleashing the Potential**: Fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, and skill development.
 
• **Green Growth**: Promoting sustainable and environmentally friendly practices.
 
• **Youth Power**: Empowering the youth through education, skill development, and employment opportunities.
 
• **Financial Sector**: Strengthening the financial sector to support inclusive growth.

questions.question: Since which year did rapid economic growth led to a sharp reduction in India's extreme poverty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1991**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1991** is the year when rapid economic growth led to a sharp reduction in India's extreme poverty.
 
• This period marked the beginning of economic liberalization in India, which included significant reforms in industrial policy, trade, and investment.
 
• The reforms were aimed at making the economy more market-oriented and expanding the role of private and foreign investment.
 
• These changes resulted in increased economic growth, job creation, and a substantial reduction in poverty levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The economic liberalization in India began with the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao and the then Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh in July **1991**.
 
• The reforms included measures such as reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing taxes, which collectively contributed to the economic growth.
 
• As a result of these reforms, India's GDP growth rate increased significantly, and the poverty rate declined from 45% in 1994 to about 21% in 2011.
 
• The liberalization policies were aimed at integrating India into the global economy and encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI).
 
• These changes not only helped in reducing poverty but also in improving the overall standard of living for many Indians.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Classification of Expenditure of government?

I. Revenue Expenditure is expenditure incurred for purposes other than the creation of physical or financial assets of the central government.

II. Capital expenditure results in creation of physical or financial assets or reduction in financial liabilities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure **refers to expenditures necessary for the **day-to-day functioning** of the government and the provision of services.
 
• These are typically** recurring expenses **aimed at maintaining current operations rather than investing in new infrastructure or assets.
 
• Revenue Expenditure is different from **Capital Expenditure**, which is spent on **creating assets or reducing liabilities**.
 
• Capital expenditure is primarily focused on long-term investments that enhance the productive capacity of the economy or strengthen the government’s financial position.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sub-categories of Revenue Expenditure:**

 
 
• **Developmental Revenue Expenditure:** Expenditure on sectors like education, healthcare, and welfare schemes.
 
• **Non-developmental Revenue Expenditure: **Administrative expenses, defense spending, and interest payments.
 
 
 
• **Sub-categories of Capital Expenditure:**
 
 
• **Developmental Capital Expenditure:**** **Investment in physical assets like roads, power plants, and schools.
 
• **Non-developmental Capital Expenditure:** Expenditure on defense equipment, repayment of loans, etc.

questions.question: The idea of __________ has been borrowed from the Constitution of erstwhile USSR (Union of Soviet Socialist Republics).

options.text: Both Fundamental Duties and Fundamental Rights

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Fundamental Duties__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **Fundamental Duties** was borrowed from the **Constitution of the erstwhile USSR**.
 
• These duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties.
 
• There are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights** in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the **Bill of Rights** in the US Constitution.
 
• The **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution was influenced by the **Objectives Resolution** drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** is also known as the **“Mini-Constitution”** due to its extensive changes to the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the Supreme Court as a court of record?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 129.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 129 states that the Supreme Court of India is a **"Court of Record."**
 
• The Court of Record status ensures that its judgments, orders, and other proceedings are preserved and can be referred to as authoritative.
 
• **Article 129** of the Indian Constitution was** part of the original Constitution** when it was enacted on **January 26, 1950**.
 
• The Supreme Court is the **apex court** of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 123** of the Indian Constitution pertains to the **President's power to make ordinances**.
 
• **Article 125 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the **salaries and allowances** of the **judges of the Supreme Court** of India.
 
• **Article 127** allows for the** appointment of ad hoc judges to the Supreme Court **if the Chief Justice of India (CJI) certifies the need.
 
• **Article 32** allows to issue of directions or orders or **writs**, including writs of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari, for the enforcement of fundamental rights
